data.name: Kelley
data.gender_notes: Kelley is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Old English ‘Ceolhene’ and Old Norse ‘Kel’, meaning ‘slender’ or ‘narrow’. In Middle English, Kelley referred to a monk or a monk’s cowl. In the Christian tradition, Kelley is associated with St. Kelley, a Celtic hermit known for his devotion and seclusion. The name Kelley carries the meaning “Slender, narrow” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Kelley usually hope their child will grow to embody slender, narrow and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes devotion, seclusion, and spiritual growth.
data.etymology: Kelley belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Slender, narrow.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kelley total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_greek.name: Κέλλυ
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Κέλλυ προέρχεται από την ελληνική παράδοση και σημαίνει χαρά του Θεού. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, παρόμοια ονόματα συνδέονται με έννοιες πνευματικής χαράς και θεϊκής εύνοιας. Το όνομα χρησιμοποιήθηκε στην πρώιμη Εκκλησία για να εκφράσει τη χαρά που προέρχεται από την πίστη.

in_latin.name: Kelley
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Kelley is derived from Latin roots associated with joy and celebration. In early Christian tradition, names similar to Kelley were used to signify happiness and divine favor. The name reflects a spiritual aspiration towards joy and contentment.

in_english.long_meaning: The name Kelley originates from Hebrew and Greek roots, signifying joy or celebration. In Christian tradition, Kelley connotes a sense of happiness and divine blessing. Historically, the name has been used across various cultures to express spiritual joy and optimism. Kelley symbolizes a cheerful and enthusiastic personality.

data.cultural_impact: The name Kelley has a rich cultural history, including its association with St. Kelley, a Celtic hermit who was known for his dedication to God and solitary lifestyle. This association with monasticism has contributed to the name being used to represent a strong sense of spiritual devotion and dedication in various Christian contexts.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Kelley holds spiritual significance as a reminder of the importance of devotion and introspection in the Christian faith. It also serves as a symbol of the contemplative life, encouraging individuals to seek a deeper connection with God through prayer, reflection, and self-discipline, just as St. Kelley did in his seclusion.
